    CHAPTER I

‘Good morning to you,’ said the baker, leaning upon his counter
with both elbows. ‘You are about early, and the sun is hardly up.’

‘I could not sleep,’ the young woman answered him. ‘There was a
great noise down in the harbour all night, and I lay awake then.’

‘They will be talking of it for a month,’ the woman said to him.

‘Such a thing has not happened here within my memory at all.’
